title: Dodge Challenger Vehicle Analysis
summary: Analysis of multiple Dodge Challengers seen at UVU on September 10, 2025. The prosecution presents surveillance footage as showing Tyler Robinson's vehicle, but comparison reveals potential discrepancies suggesting more than one Challenger was present.

robinsons_confirmed_vehicle.wheels: Full chrome 5-spoke wheels with distinctive polished finish
robinsons_confirmed_vehicle.front_plate: No visible front license plate bracket

surveillance_vehicles.source: Surveillance footage (yellow box comparison collage - left side)
surveillance_vehicles.color: Dark-colored, difficult to determine precisely due to low-light/resolution
surveillance_vehicles.wheels: Cannot confirm as matching chrome 5-spokes - proportions and reflections appear different
surveillance_vehicles.front_bumper: Different lower grille/fascia configuration visible in yellow-box highlighted area
surveillance_vehicles.rear: Taillights visible, bumper/diffuser proportions warrant scrutiny

surveillance_vehicles.wheels: Silver/machined-face wheels - DIFFERENT style from confirmed vehicle's full chrome
surveillance_vehicles.notes: Used as prosecution reference but wheel style doesn't match Robinson's confirmed car
Appears similar to driveway photo but angle and lighting make precise comparison difficult

key_discrepancies.detail: Robinson's confirmed car has full chrome wheels. Some comparison images show machined-face or different spoke-pattern wheels. This is one of the most reliable distinguishing features between Challenger trims.
Lower front bumper area varies between images. Different trim levels (SE, SXT, R/T, SRT) have noticeably different front bumper designs, fog light surrounds, and grille inserts.

At least two different shades of gray/dark appear across surveillance footage. One closer to Tungsten Metallic, another could be Granite Crystal or darker. Low-light surveillance makes this harder but tones don't consistently match.
Some Challengers have functional or decorative hood scoops depending on trim. Surveillance resolution too low to confirm, but hood profiles aren't obviously identical across all shots.

surveillance_black_shirt.clothing: Black long-sleeve shirt with eagle/American flag graphic
surveillance_black_shirt.accessories: Dark cap, sunglasses, black backpack, Converse-style sneakers

surveillance_red_shirt.distinguishing: Appears to have compression sleeve or brace on one leg - verifiable detail
surveillance_red_shirt.note: When not cropped or compressed, proportions could reasonably be a different person

person_comparison.distortion_concern: Surveillance cameras use wide-angle lenses that distort proportions. Compressing or cropping further changes apparent body proportions, face shape, and build. Can create false visual similarity that wouldn't hold up under proper aspect-ratio comparison.

conclusion: At least 2-3 different Challenger configurations appear across the images based on wheel styles, front fascia details, and possible color differences. A university parking lot could easily have multiple Challengers of this generation. Proper forensic image analysis preserving original aspect ratios would be needed for definitive comparison.
recommendations: Obtain original NVR footage files with native resolution and aspect ratio
Compare VIN-specific features if any are visible (wheel bolt pattern, specific trim badges)
Document every Challenger registration in UVU parking records for Sept 10
Compare license plate visibility across all footage
Forensic image analyst should determine original aspect ratios before identification comparison
